extracted.intended_audience: USPTO examiners, patent practitioners, and applicants dealing with national security, secrecy orders, and foreign filing
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and substantive standards governing handling of security-marked patent papers, examination and prosecution of Secrecy Order cases, requirements and scope for foreign filing licenses, petitions (including retroactive), export-control interactions, and penalties. Intended to ensure patent practice complies with national security and export-control law and PTO regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling of applications and papers bearing security markings
rubrics_metrics.description: Papers marked as prescribed in the Executive Orders and showing such marking applied by or at the direction of a government agency are accepted in patent applications; however, all applications or papers bearing words such as “Secret” or “Confidential” must be promptly referred to Technology Center (TC) Working Group 3640 for clarification or security treatment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Under no circumstances may any such application, drawing, exhibit, or other paper be placed in public records (e.g., patented files) until all security markings have been considered and declassified or otherwise explained. Authorized security markings may be placed on patent application drawings when filed provided such markings are outside the illustrations and are removed when the material is declassified (37 CFR 1.84(v)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Examination location and transfer of Secrecy Order cases
rubrics_metrics.description: All applications in which a Secrecy Order has been imposed are examined in Technology Center (TC) Working Group 3640 and Art Unit 3662; if a Secrecy Order is imposed after docketing in another TC, the application will be transferred to TC Working Group 3640.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Secrecy Order cases are examined for patentability as other cases, but special handling rules (e.g., restrictions on issuing patents or declaring interferences) apply. Examiners in WG3640/Art Unit 3662 will conduct interference searches for classified/Secrecy Order cases when requested by outside examiners.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restrictions on issuance and interferences for Secrecy Order cases
rubrics_metrics.description: Secrecy Order cases may not be passed to issue while under order; nor will an interference be declared where one or more conflicting cases is classified or under Secrecy Order (see MPEP § 2309.06).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When requested, examiners in WG3640/Art Unit 3662 will perform interference searches of files containing briefcards from classified or Secrecy Order cases. These procedural limits are tied to security classification until declassification/rescission of the Order.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeal and hearing limitations while Secrecy Order in effect
rubrics_metrics.description: In case of a final rejection, the applicant must reply and, if an appeal is filed, must complete it to prevent abandonment; however, the appeal will not be set for hearing by the Board of Patent Appeals and Interferences until the Secrecy Order is removed unless specifically ordered by the Commissioner for Patents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must pursue procedural steps to preserve rights (e.g., timely appeals), but substantive Board hearings are withheld while secrecy restrictions remain in effect except upon Commissioner direction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allowance notice and treatment of post-allowance amendments under Secrecy Order
rubrics_metrics.description: When a Secrecy Order case is in condition for allowance, a notice of allowability (Form D-10) is issued, closing prosecution; amendments received thereafter are not entered or responded to until the Secrecy Order is rescinded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Upon rescission, amendments that are free from objection will be entered; otherwise they will be denied entry. This preserves prosecution closure while security status persists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Setting of reply periods in Secrecy Order cases
rubrics_metrics.description: Due to additional administrative burdens associated with handling papers in Secrecy Order cases, the full statutory period for reply will ordinarily be set for all Office actions issued on such cases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiners should account for extra processing time when setting periods to reply; applicants receive full statutory time rather than shortened periods normally used in some cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling of applications bearing national-security markings but no Secrecy Order
rubrics_metrics.description: If an application bears national security markings but no Secrecy Order has been issued, the examiner should require the applicant to seek imposition of a Secrecy Order or authority to cancel the markings, preferably in the first action and prior to final disposition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pursuant to 37 CFR 5.1(d), if no Secrecy Order has issued the Office will set a time period within which the applicant must (A) obtain a Secrecy Order; (B) declassify the application; or (C) submit evidence of a good faith effort to obtain a Secrecy Order pursuant to 37 CFR 5.2(a) to prevent abandonment. Per 37 CFR 5.1(e) the application will not be allowed until declassified and any Secrecy Order rescinded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Foreign filing license requirement (35 U.S.C. 184 / 37 CFR 5.11)
rubrics_metrics.description: A license from the Commissioner for Patents under 35 U.S.C. 184 is required before filing any application for patent (including modifications, amendments, supplements, or divisions) in a foreign patent office or international agency when the invention was made in the United States and (1) a U.S. application has been filed less than six months prior to the foreign filing date, or (2) no U.S. application has been filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The term 'application' includes modifications, amendments, supplements, and divisions. Licenses may be granted retroactively in narrow circumstances (e.g., filing abroad through error without deceptive intent and not disclosing inventions within scope of §181). The Commissioner shall prescribe implementing regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of a foreign filing license (37 CFR 5.15)
rubrics_metrics.description: A license may authorize export and filing of duplicate/formal application papers abroad; making amendments, modifications, supplements (including divisions and supporting matter) that consist of illustration, exemplification, comparison, or explanation of subject matter disclosed in the application; and taking actions in prosecution of the foreign or international application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The license only authorizes such acts so long as the additions do not change the general nature of the invention in a manner that would require the U.S. application to have been made available for inspection under 35 U.S.C. 181. The license does not permit inclusion of technical data pertaining to (i) defense services/articles on the U.S. Munitions List or (ii) Restricted Data/sensitive nuclear technology restricted by Atomic Energy Act / Nuclear Non-Proliferation Act (see 37 CFR 5.15(a)(3)). Paragraphs (a) and (b) distinguish scope depending on whether the material was required to be made available under 35 U.S.C.181.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petitions for foreign filing licenses and required contents (37 CFR 5.12–5.14)
rubrics_metrics.description: Filing a U.S. application is considered to include an implicit petition for a foreign filing license; if the automatic petition is not granted, a subsequent petition (37 CFR 5.12(b)) may be filed and must include the fee (§1.17(h)), petitioner’s address, and delivery instructions for the license.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If no corresponding U.S. application exists, the petition must be accompanied by a legible copy of the material (37 CFR 5.13). If a corresponding U.S. application exists, the petition must identify that application by number, filing date, inventor, and title but need not include a copy (37 CFR 5.14). If the foreign filing will contain matter not disclosed in the U.S. application(s), a copy of the foreign application or detailed identification of new matter must be furnished (37 CFR 5.14(c)). Explicit petitions may be faxed to Licensing and Review; the filing receipt indicates if an implicit license was granted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conversion of narrow-scope licenses to broad scope (37 CFR 5.15(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants granted a license under 37 CFR 5.12(b) with the relatively narrow scope of 5.15(b) may petition under 5.15(c) to convert the license to the broader scope of 5.15(a) by payment of a fee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No such petition will be granted if the material filed pursuant to 5.13 or any corresponding U.S. application was required to be made available for inspection under 35 U.S.C.181. If granted, the change in scope is effective on the date of grant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Revocation of foreign filing license and its effects (37 CFR 5.11(f) and discussion)
rubrics_metrics.description: A license pursuant to 37 CFR 5.11(a) can be revoked at any time upon written notification by the PTO; revocation becomes effective on the date the notice is mailed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Revocation ordinarily indicates referral to defense agencies for additional review. Revocation of a filing-receipt license does not necessarily preclude grant of a petition under 5.12(b) for a narrower license. Foreign filings that occurred prior to revocation need not be abandoned, but additional filings without a license are not permitted unless six months have elapsed from the filing of any corresponding U.S. application. The imposition of a Secrecy Order will cause revocation of the six-month authority arising from 35 U.S.C.184.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition for retroactive license requirements (37 CFR 5.25)
rubrics_metrics.description: A petition for a retroactive license under 35 U.S.C.184 must be presented per §5.13 or §5.14(a) and include: (1) listing of each foreign country in which unlicensed material was filed; (2) dates of filing in each country; (3) a verified statement (oath/declaration) containing (i) averment that the subject matter was not under a secrecy order at time of filing abroad and is not currently under a secrecy order, (ii) a showing that the license has been diligently sought after discovery of the proscribed foreign filing, and (iii) an explanation why material was filed abroad through error and without deceptive intent; and (4) the required fee (§1.17(h)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Retroactive licenses are only made retroactive with respect to specific acts of foreign filing, so precise countries, dates, and circumstances must be provided. The verified statement must be in oath or declaration form.

rubrics_metrics.name: Penalties and forfeiture for unlicensed foreign filing and disclosure (35 U.S.C. 184–186)
rubrics_metrics.description: Notwithstanding other law, a person shall not receive a U.S. patent for an invention if that person filed in a foreign country without procuring the license prescribed in §184; such a U.S. patent shall be invalid unless the failure to procure the license was through error and without deceptive intent and the patent does not disclose subject matter within the scope of §181. Additionally, willful publication/disclosure during a secrecy order or willful filing abroad without required license can result in fines up to $10,000 or imprisonment for up to two years, or both.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These provisions apply to patents and applications before, on, or after specified enactment dates; courts may provide equitable remedies for parties who reasonably relied on prior invalidity/unenforceability (per Public Law 100-418 provisions). Penalties are separate from administrative revocation of licenses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interaction with export-control regulations (ITAR, EAR, DOE)
rubrics_metrics.description: Export of technical data and patent-related activities are subject to restrictions administered by Departments of State, Commerce, and Energy; compliance with PTO regulations under 35 U.S.C.184 may authorize certain exports without separate Department of State approval unless exporting technical data exceeding that used to support a patent application in a foreign country.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 37 CFR 5.11(b–c) explains that a PTO license may authorize export of technical data for preparation/filing/prosecution of a foreign patent application without separately complying with 22 CFR parts 121–130 (ITAR), 15 CFR part 779 (EAR), and 10 CFR part 810, provided conditions are met. 37 CFR 5.18 clarifies that if a patent applicant complies with PTO regulations, no separate State Dept. approval is required unless exporting technical data beyond that used to support the patent application (22 CFR part 125). 37 CFR 5.19 and 5.20 state that Department of Commerce and DOE regulations provide related exceptions and that an application eligible for foreign filing under 35 U.S.C.184 may be considered information available to the public for DOE purposes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exportation rules for specific subject matter (arms, sensitive nuclear technology)
rubrics_metrics.description: Technical data relating to arms, ammunition, and implements of war are generally subject to ITAR (22 CFR parts 120–130) and the U.S. Munitions List; restricted data and sensitive nuclear technology are governed by Atomic Energy Act / DOE regulations (10 CFR part 810).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the patent applicant complies with PTO regulations under 35 U.S.C.184, no separate Department of State approval is required unless the applicant seeks to export technical data exceeding that used to support a patent application in a foreign country. For Secrecy Order cases subject to §5.2, a petition under §5.5 to permit filing abroad removes need for a separate State Dept. request (22 CFR part 125). DOE regulations (10 CFR 810.7) treat properly filed patent applications eligible for foreign filing under 35 U.S.C.184 as publicly available information for DOE regulation purposes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preservation of confidentiality and statements to DOE/NASA (37 CFR 1.14; 42 U.S.C.2182 and 42 U.S.C.2457)
rubrics_metrics.description: For inventions useful in production/utilization of special nuclear material or atomic energy, applicants must file, with the application or within thirty days after request, a sworn statement setting forth the full facts surrounding making/conception and whether the invention was made or conceived in the course of or under any contract, subcontract, or arrangement with or for the benefit of the Commission (42 U.S.C.2182). Similarly, for inventions significant to aeronautical/space activities (42 U.S.C.2457) a written statement under oath describing the circumstances of creation and relationship to any Administration contract must be filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Director forwards copies of the application and the statement to the Commission or Administrator as appropriate when the application is in condition for allowance. These statutory statements preserve governmental interests and ensure DOE/NASA are notified of sensitive inventions.
